body:
The readable decoder copied valid large documents into whole-document character arrays before parsing. JavaScript could fail before restoring any of the consumer's 1,764 historical records. Decode directly from the input string and use native quote searches/slices across JavaScript, Rust, Python and C#. Preserve the existing grammar, Unicode, legacy doubled quotes, n-quote closing runs, escaped markers and strict malformed-input rejection.

Escaped values now use fresh strict incremental UTF-8 decoders with bounded byte buffers in JavaScript, Python and C#. Rust already converts its output byte buffer directly into the returned string, so it needs no second temporary byte buffer. No runtime library was added.

The [complete requirement mapping, alternative solutions, implementation plan and primary-source research](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/blob/issue-69-dab96606bd2e/docs/case-studies/issue-68/README.md) covers #69, #68 and all comments. The repository-wide repair addresses the equivalent allocations in all four implementations.

### Reproduction and automated verification

- Run `node --expose-gc --max-old-space-size=768 experiments/issue-68/large-document.mjs document`. The offline regression generates **149,255,115 UTF-8 bytes and 1,764 records**, restores every record, checks each JSON and legacy compact round trip, and verifies the complete re-encoded SHA-256. It fails on the original JavaScript decoder and passes after this repair.
- Long quoted and escaped values run in separate **128 MiB heap** children. The JS suite runs all three probes with a finite test deadline. Python and C# add allocation regressions; all four languages test Unicode quote runs, UTF-8 chunk boundaries and malformed escapes.
- The original Node 22.23.3 decoder exhausts a bounded 768 MiB heap on a separate 144,497,778-byte padded valid document. For a 33,555,493-byte padded document, peak RSS falls from 630,296 KiB to 122,360 KiB. The consumer's exact default-heap `RangeError` was not reproduced locally; the avoided allocation and limited-heap failure were reproduced.
- Local full suites: **JS 516; Python 514 (91% coverage); Rust 127 with all features and 123 without default features; C# 540**. All **16 cross-language writer/reader pairings** agree. Shared/release/dependency tooling tests also pass.
- Lint, formatting, duplication, warnings-as-errors, file-size, parser parity, release-fragment/version gates, dependency freshness and package assembly checks pass locally. Rust builds ran sequentially with one build job and debug info disabled under the container memory limit.

The original private archive was not supplied. The synthetic regression matches its historical-record count and exceeds its reported notation size without network requests. The [consumer receipt](https://github.com/konard/lazada-search/blob/c7149901c1877c12cc6a08c4e65ed0a42dd58224/docs/acceptance/source-integrity/codec-large-document.json) independently validates the same scanning approach on the actual archive. Binary/blob conversion is a consumer API; no history is removed or decoding bypassed here. The codec still holds input and decoded output in memory; this change does not introduce a streaming API.

### CI and release preparation

Initial CI failed because C# pinned parser 0.25.1 while the other implementations pinned 0.23.0, and freshness checks found stale dependencies. Align all implementations and maintained dependency probes on **links-notation 0.25.2**, refresh shipping/probe lockfiles and current development dependencies, and retain every CI gate. The dependency update requires **Rust 1.87**; development tests require **1.88**. Rust's fragment requests a minor release because its compiler floor increased. JS requests an automated patch release; Python and C# prepare unpublished version **0.3.1**.

Fixes #69
Fixes #68
title: Decode large readable documents without character arrays
